title: What happens when you go to a website
goal: You can explain, in order, what happens between clicking a link and seeing a page.
self_check: Say the six steps out loud in order. What did the server actually send back?
fix_this: No broken code — instead, open the Network tab and count the requests one page makes.

title: The pieces a website is made of
goal: You can name the three languages a web page is made of, and say what each one is for.
self_check: Which of the three could make a button react to a click? Which two could not, however well written?
fix_this: A page where the colours have gone but the words are still there. Which file is missing?

title: What is a dish?
goal: You can say what every dish on your menu needs to have.
self_check: Could someone write your menu from your list without asking you anything?
fix_this: A dish with no price and a description that just says 'yummy'.

title: What a tag is
goal: You can write a tag, and you know why the browser needs you to.
self_check:
Does every `

` you wrote have a matching `

`? Can you see any angle brackets on the page itself? You should not be able to.
new_things:
`

`, angle brackets, opening and closing tags, the slash
fix_this: A page with four separate lines of writing and no tags at all — the browser runs them together into one line. Wrap each in its own paragraph.

title: Your first page
goal: You can make words appear in a browser.
self_check: Do your words appear? Is your restaurant's name in the browser tab?
fix_this: A page where the restaurant name is inside `<title>` and the `<body>` is empty. The page is blank — but the name IS in the browser tab. Where did it go?

title: Headings big and small
goal: You can break your page into parts with headings.
self_check: Read only your headings top to bottom. Do they work as an outline on their own?
fix_this: A page where every single line is an `<h1>`, so nothing looks more important than anything else. Give it a proper heading order.

title: Lists
goal: You can make a list where each item sits on its own line.
self_check: Does each item sit on its own line with a bullet?
fix_this: A list with the `<li>` tags missing, so it all runs together.

title: Putting one tag inside another
goal: You can nest tags without tangling them.
self_check: Does every open tag have its partner, in reverse order?
fix_this: A list where each `<ul>` is opened inside the one before it and never closed. Every item marches further right with a different bullet. Where does each list end?

title: Pictures
goal: You can put a picture on your page and describe it for people who cannot see it.
self_check: If the image file vanished, would the alt text still tell you what was there?
fix_this: An `` with a filename that does not exist, and one with no alt.

title: Links
goal: You can send someone somewhere else, and you know how to write the address.
self_check: Read just the blue words with the sentence covered. Do you still know where each goes?
fix_this: A link saying 'click here', and one to another site missing its https://.

title: Checking your HTML
goal: You can find a broken tag before anyone else does.
self_check: Zero errors? And does the page still look right afterwards?
fix_this:
One unclosed `

` that the browser silently repairs, so the page LOOKS fine. Only the validator finds it.

title: Connecting a stylesheet
goal: Your colours live in a different file from your words.
self_check: Delete style.css. Did the page go plain? If not, your CSS is in the wrong place.
fix_this: The link says styles.css but the file is called style.css.

title: What a rule looks like
goal: You can read any piece of CSS and name its three parts.
self_check: Can you point at all three parts in a rule you did not write?
fix_this: A rule missing a semicolon and a closing bracket.

title: Colour
goal: You can set the colour of any words or any background.
self_check: Stand back two metres. Can you still read every part of your page?
fix_this: Pale grey text on white. Can you read it from across the room?

title: Lettering and size
goal: You can change which lettering your page uses and how big it is.
self_check: Is your smallest text comfortable for a seven-year-old?
fix_this: font-family: Trebuchet MS, sans-serif — missing its quote marks.

title: Choosing what to change
goal: You can style every paragraph, or only the ones you picked.
self_check: Did only the things you meant to change actually change?
new_things: tag selectors, class selectors, class attribute
fix_this: CSS saying price { } with no dot, and HTML saying class=".price" with one.

title: Padding, border and margin
goal: You can put space around anything on your page.
self_check: Add a temporary border. Can you see where the box actually ends?
fix_this: A box with padding and margin swapped. Which one moved the neighbours?

title: One side at a time
goal: You can put space on just the top, or just the left.
self_check: Exactly one line above each dish, and none anywhere else?
fix_this: A dish list where the line lands under the description instead of above the name.

title: Putting things in the middle
goal: You can centre the page, and centre a picture.
self_check: Widen the browser window. Does your page stay centred?
fix_this: A picture with margin: 0 auto that will not move. It needs display: block.

title: Sizing pictures
goal: You can size a picture without squashing it.
self_check: Does the picture look like the real thing, not stretched?
fix_this: A logo with both set wrong, so it looks stretched.

title: When nothing happens
goal: You can work out why your CSS is being ignored.
self_check: Put background-color: gold on body. No gold means the link is the problem, not your rule.
fix_this: One missing } stopping every rule below it from working.

title: Writing criteria a partner can test
goal: You can write down what 'finished' means so someone else can check it without asking you.
self_check: Hand it to a partner. Did they get through it without asking you anything?
fix_this: A criterion saying 'the menu should look nice'. Rewrite it so two people would agree.

title: Writing a bug report
goal: You can report a problem so precisely someone else can see it themselves.
self_check: Could someone follow your steps and see the same problem without you there?
fix_this: A report saying 'the page is broken'.

title: Giving useful feedback
goal: You can say what is wrong with a page without being unkind or vague.
self_check: Does it name one thing, on one part of the page, that could actually be changed?
fix_this: Feedback saying 'the colours are bad'. Rewrite so the author knows what to change.

title: Grouping things together
goal: You can put several tags inside one container so they move and style as one.
self_check: Add a temporary border to your div. Does it wrap exactly what you meant?
fix_this: Every dish needs a background colour, but there is nothing to put it on.

title: Photographs that load fast
goal: You can add real photos of your dishes without making the page slow.
self_check: Does the whole page appear in under two seconds?
fix_this: A page with three huge photos. Time how long it takes to appear.

title: A colour scheme that works
goal: Your colours look deliberate and everyone can read them.
self_check: Does every text colour pass the contrast checker against what is behind it?
fix_this: A palette where the price colour fails contrast against the background.

title: Type that guides the eye
goal: Someone can find what they want without reading everything.
self_check: Ask someone to find the cheapest vegetarian dish. Time them. Under 30 seconds?
fix_this: A menu where dish names and descriptions are the same size and weight.

title: Side by side
goal: You can put two things next to each other instead of stacked.
self_check: Do name and price align at the same edge on every single dish?
fix_this: A dish where the name and price will not share a line.

title: Showing something can be clicked
goal: Your links look different under the mouse and under the keyboard.
self_check: Tab through the whole page. Can you always see where you are?
fix_this: A page with :hover only. Now reach the link using nothing but Tab.

title: Fits any screen
goal: Your menu works on a phone as well as a laptop.
self_check: Drag the window from very narrow to very wide. Does anything overlap or fall off?
fix_this: A layout that looks right on a laptop and breaks completely at phone width.

title: More than one page
goal: You can build a site of several pages that link to each other.
self_check: From any page, can you reach every other page without the back button?
fix_this: A second page with no way back to the first.

title: Your first script
goal: You can run some JavaScript from your page.
self_check: Does your message appear in the console?
fix_this: A script tag pointing at a file that does not exist. Nothing happens, nothing complains.

title: Finding something on the page
goal: You can reach into the page from JavaScript and change something.
self_check: Did the thing on the page change when you reloaded?
fix_this: A script that runs before the page has loaded, so it finds nothing.

title: Responding to a click
goal: Something on your page reacts when a visitor clicks it.
self_check: Write down what should happen before you click. Did exactly that happen?
fix_this: A button wired to the wrong element, so clicking does nothing.

title: Show and hide
goal: A visitor can open and close parts of your menu.
self_check: Click twice. Are you back where you started?
fix_this: A show/hide button that hides but will not bring anything back.

title: Adding up an order
goal: A visitor can choose dishes and see the total.
self_check: Add three dishes and remove one. Does the total match what you work out on paper?
fix_this: A total showing 12.300000000000001 instead of 12.30.

title: Remembering what they chose
goal: Your page keeps track of what the visitor has done so far.
self_check: Do a dozen random clicks. Does the screen still match the underlying numbers?
fix_this: A page where the display and the real total quietly disagree.

title: The menu as a list of data
goal: Your dishes live in a list in JavaScript instead of being typed into the HTML.
self_check: Is every dish in the list, with the same fields, spelled the same way every time?
fix_this: A dish object missing its price. What should happen to it?

title: Building the page from the data
goal: The HTML for your dishes is written by your code, not by you.
self_check: Add a dish to the list only. Does it appear without you touching the HTML?
fix_this: A loop that only ever shows the last dish.

title: When the data is wrong
goal: Your page copes with a dish that is missing something.
self_check: Delete a field from one dish. Does the page still look deliberate?
fix_this: A dish with no description, printing 'undefined' on the page for everyone to see.

title: Filtering
goal: A visitor can choose to see only some of the dishes.
self_check: Choose each filter. Does the number of dishes shown match what you counted by hand?
fix_this: A filter that hides everything, because the tag names do not match the data.

title: Sorting
goal: A visitor can put the menu in price order.
self_check: Sort by price. Read the prices top to bottom. Are they really in order?
fix_this: A price sort that puts $10.00 before $9.00.

title: One file, many pages
goal: The same data file fills more than one page of your site.
self_check: Change one price in the data file. Did it change everywhere it appears?
fix_this: Two pages with two copies of the data that have drifted apart.
